Section  9. Magistrates and constables; appointment; com­
pensation. —There shall be a magistrate and a constable for 
each of the towns of Balboa and Cristobal, who shall be ap­
pointed, and whose compensation shall be fixed, by the Gov­
ernor; and in the event of the absence or disability of a 
magistrate or constable, the Governor may appoint an addi­
tional magistrate or constable to serve during such absence 
or disability.
Cross-References
Appointment, term, and compensation of magistrates, 
constables, and other employees, see Code, title 7, section 4.
Oath of magistrates and constables, see Code, title 7, 
section 5.
Section  10. Places of holding magistrates? courts. —The 
magistrates shall hold court at such places in their respective 
towns as may be designated from time to time by the 
Governor.
Cross-Reference
Authority of President to prescribe times and places of 
holding magistrates’  courts, see Code, title 7, section 6.
S ection  11. Bonds of constables. —The constables ap­
pointed for the magistrates’ courts shall be required before 
assuming office to execute a bond with two or more good 
and sufficient sureties, or with a corporate surety, to be 
approved by the Governor, in the sum of $1000, conditioned 
that the officer executing the bond will faithfully comply 
with his duties as constable, and will turn over all money, 
property, and effects coming into his hands by virtue of his 
office, to the persons entitled thereto in accordance with law. 
The bond may be sued upon in any court of competent 
jurisdiction by any person who may be injured by reason 
of a failure of official duty on the part of the constable. 
The bond shall not become void upon a first recovery but 
successive suits may be instituted thereon until the full 
amount thereof is exhausted.
Cross-References
Authority of President to regulate bonds of constables, 
see Code, title 7, section 6.
For provisions respecting corporate sureties on bonds, 
see Code, title 4, section 962.
Section  12. Duties of constables. —The constables of the 
magistrates’  courts shall:
(a) Attend all sessions of the magistrate’ s court for the 
town and subdivision to which they may be assigned by 
the Governor.
(b) Preserve order in the court.
(c) Receive and receipt for all money collected by them 
upon any process or paid into or deposited with the magis­
trate’ s court as fees, fines, costs, forfeitures, or bail.
(d) Duly account for such money in accordance with 
rules and regulations to be prescribed by the Governor.
Cross-References
Authority of President to prescribe the duties of con­
stables and the disposition of fines, costs, and forfeitures, 
see Code, title 7, section 6.
Payment of all fees over to Collector of Panama Canal, 
see Code, title A, section 981, as amended by act of May 
13, 1936, 49 Stat. 1269.
Section  13. Prior orders superseded. —This order super­
sedes Executive Orders dated March 12, 1914 (No. 1898), 
August 3, 1914 (No. 2007), February 26, 1924 (No. 3965), 
May 25, 1927, August 29, 1927 (No. 4711), January 3, 1928 
(No. 4792), September 2, 1931 (No. 5704), November 3, 1933 
(No. 6390), and all other Executive Orders heretofore issued 
which relate to the Canal Zone judiciary and are of a 
permanent and continuing nature.

By virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the act of June 25, 1910, ch. 421, 36 Stat. 847, as amended by the act of August 24, 1912, ch. 369, 37 Stat. 497, and as President of the United States, and in order to effectuate further the purposes of the Upper Mississippi River Wild Life and Fish Refuge Act (43 Stat. 650), and the Migratory Bird Conservation Act (45 Stat. 1222), it is ordered that the following-described lands, comprising 4,266.62 acres, more or less, in Winona and Wabasha Counties, Minnesota, and Buffalo County, Wisconsin, situated on either side of, or upon islands in, the Mississippi River between Rock Island, Illinois, and Wabasha, Minnesota, and subject to overflow by said River, which lands have been determined by the Secretary of Agriculture to be suitable for the purposes of said Upper Mississippi River Wild Life and Fish Refuge Act, be, and they are hereby, reserved and set apart, subject to valid existing rights, for the use of the Department of Agriculture as a breeding place for migratory and other wild birds, game and fur-bearing animals, and fish and other aquatic animal life, and for the conservation of wild flowers and aquatic plants, to be administered as a part of the Upper Mississippi River Wild Life and Fish Refuge.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

THE WHITE HOUSE,

### Tfb0b82df324e5d7285fa62bd

Text hash 5cb683e1a60eb17384abef0443b63e499d307c038eff3e8dc3977e9f119d7123; absolute characters 0–990; files: jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-7502-withdrawal-public-land-for-administrative-site-california.txt

```text
By virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the act of June 25, 1910, ch. 421, 36 Stat. 847, as amended by the act of August 24, 1912, ch. 369, 37 Stat. 497, it is ordered as follows:

Section 1. Executive Order No. 6910 of November 26, 1934, as amended, temporarily withdrawing certain lands for classification and other purposes, is hereby revoked as to the following-described tract of public land in California:

MOUNT DIABLO MERIDIAN

T. 9 S., R. 1 E., sec. 34, lot 3, 9.21 acres.

Section 2. Subject to valid existing rights, the tract of land described in section 1 of this order is hereby temporarily withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserved for use as an administrative site in connection with Federal and State cooperative forestprotection work.

Section 3. Section 2 of this order shall continue in force and effect unless and until revoked by the President or by act of Congress.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

THE WHITE HOUSE,

December 3, 1936.

```

Maritime Commission, and other govern­
ment procurement agencies, which are 
hereby directed to cooperate with and es­
tablish close liaison with such Division 
to accomplish the purposes of this order.
9. The Defense Contract Service, es­
tablished pursuant to Regulation No. 9, 
July 29, 1941,1  of the Office of Production 
Management, is hereby abolished. The 
duties and responsibilities of said Defense 
Contract Service are hereby assigned to 
tie  Division of Contract Distribution. 
All records, files, and equipment of the 
Defense Contract Service shall be trans­
ferred to the Division of Contract Dis­
tribution.
F ranklin  D R oosevelt
T he  W hite  H ouse ,
September 4, 1941.
[No. 8891]
[F. R. Doc. 41-6703; Filed, September 5, 1941;
2:49 p. m.J
EXECUTIVE ORDER
Establishing  the  O ffice  of D efense  
H ealth  and W elfare S ervices  in  the  
E xecutive  O ffice  of th e P resident  
and D efining  its  F unctions  and D uties
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by the Constitution and statutes of 
the United States, and in order to define 
further the functions and duties of the 
Office for Emergency Management of the 
Executive Office of the President with 
respect to the national emergency as de­
clared by the President on May 27,1941,“  
for the purpose of assuring adequate 
health and welfare services to meet needs 
of the national defense program, it is 
hereby ordered:
1. The term “health and welfare serv­
ices” as used in this Order means all 
health, welfare, medical, nutrition, recre­
ation, and related services including those 
aspects of education under the jurisdic­
tion of the Federal Security Agency.
2. There is established within the Of­
fice for Emergency Management of the 
Executive Office of the President the 
Office of Defense Health and Welfare 
Services, at the head of which the Fed­
eral Security Administrator shall serve 
as Director. The Director shall discharge 
and perform his responsibilities and 
duties under the direction and supervi-
1  6 F.R. 3889. 
»6 F.R. 2617.
sion of the President. The Director shall 
receive no salary or other remuneration 
as such, but shall be entitled to actual 
and necessary transportation, subsistence, 
and other expenses incidental to the per­
formance of his duties.
3. Subject to such policies, regulations, 
and directions as the President may from 
time to time prescribe, the Office shall:
a. Serve as the center for the coordina­
tion of health and welfare services made 
available by the departments and agen­
cies of the Federal Government, and 
other agencies public and private, to meet 
the needs of State and local communities 
arising from the defense program; and 
take necessary steps to secure the co­
operation of the appropriate Federal de­
partments and agencies relative thereto.
b. Make available to States and locali­
ties, upon request, the services of special­
ists in health and welfare activities to 
assist in the planning and execution of 
such local and State programs.
c. Study, plan, and encourage meas­
ures designed to assure the provision of 
adequate defense health and welfare 
services to the citizens of the Nation 
during the period of the emergency, and 
coordinate studies and surveys made by 
Federal departments and agencies with 
respect to these fields.
d. Keep the President informed with 
respect to progress made in carrying out 
this Order; and perform such related 
duties as the President may from time 
to time assign or delegate to it.
4. The Director may provide for the 
internal organization and management 
of the Office of Defense Health and Wel­
fare Services. He shall obtain the Presi­
dent’ s approval for the establishment of 
the principal subdivisions of the Office 
and the appointment of the heads 
thereof.
5. In the study of problems and in 
the discharge of its functions and re­
sponsibilities it shall be the policy of the 
Office of Defense Health and Welfare 
Services to collaborate with and to util­
ize, in so far as practicable, the facilities 
and services of existing departments and 
agencies which perform related func­
tions. Furthermore, it shall be the pol­
icy of the Office of Defense Health and 
Welfare Services in carrying out its 
functions and duties to work with and 
through the State and local defense 
councils and other appropriate State and 
local agencies, and in this connection to 
cooperate and work in conjunction with 
the Office of Civilian Defense in its rela­
tionships with State and local groups.
6. There shall be in the Office of De­
fense Health and Welfare Services a 
Health and Medical Committee to con­
sist of a Chairman to be appointed by 
the President, the Surgeon General of 
the Army, the Surgeon General of the 
Navy, the Surgeon General of the United 
States Public Health Service, the Chair­
man of the Committee on Medical Re­
search of the Office of Scientific Research 
and Development, and such others as 
the President may from time to time
determine. The Committee shall ad­
vise the Director regarding the health 
and medical aspects of national defense 
exclusive of medical research and 
assist in the coordination of health 
and medical activities affecting national 
defense. The members of the Commit­
tee shall serve as such without compen­
sation but shall be entitled to actual and 
necessary transportation, subsistence, 
and other expenses incidental to the per­
formance of their duties.
7. The Director is authorized to ap­
point such advisory committees and sub­
committees, with respect to particular 
aspects of health, welfare, nutrition, rec­
reation, and related activities as he may 
find necessary or desirable to assist him 
in the performance of his duties. Such 
advisory committees may include repre­
sentatives from Federal departments and 
agencies, State and local governments, 
private organizations and the public at 
large. The members of advisory com­
mittees shall serve as such without com­
pensation, but shall be entitled to actual 
and necessary transportation, subsist­
ence, and other expenses incidental to 
the performance of their duties.
8. Within the limits of such funds as 
may be appropriated or allocated to the 
Office of Defense Health arid Welfare 
Services by the President, the Director 
may employ necessary personnel and 
make provision for the necessary sup­
plies, facilities, and services through the 
Federal Security Agency. The Office 
of Defense Health and Welfare Services 
may use such statistical, informational, 
fiscal, personnel, and other general busi­
ness services and facilities as may be 
made available through the Office for 
Emergency Management.
F ranklin  D R oosevelt
T he  W hite  H ouse ,
Sept. 3,1941.

CHAPTER VII—AGRICULTURAL AD­
JUSTMENT ADMINISTRATION

SUBPART C— 1941
Regulations Pertaining to Wheat Mar­
keting Quotas for the 1941 Crop of  
Wheat
By virtue of the authority vested in the 
Secretary of Agriculture by Title III of 
the Agricultural Adjustment Act of 1938 
(Public Law No. 430, 75th Congress, ap­
proved February 16, 1938; 52 Stat. 31; 
7 U.S.C. 1301 et seq .), as amended, and 
Public Law No. 74, 77th Congress, ap­
proved May 26,1941, the regulations per­
taining to wheat marketing quotas for 
the 1941 crop year (form Wheat 507) 
are amended as follows:
Paragraph (a), §  728.2512  is amended 
to read as follows:
§  728.251 Payment of penalties by  
producers—(a) Producers liable for pay­
ment of penalties.  Each producer hav­
ing an interest in the wheat produced in 
1941 on any farm for which a farm mar­
keting excess is determined shall be liable 
to pay the amount of the penalty on the 
farm marketing excess. The amount of 
the penalty which any producer shall pay 
shall nevertheless be reduced by the 
amount of the penalty which is paid by 
another producer or a buyer of wheat 
produced on the farm. The amount of 
the penalty for which any producer shall 
remain liable shall be reduced to that 
proportion of the entire penalty on the 
farm marketing excess which his share 
in the 1941 crop of wheat on the farm 
bears to the total 1941 crop of wheat on 
the farm where it is determined that (1) 
the share of such producer in the wheat 
crop will be handled by or for him sep­
arately from the share of any other pro­
ducer on the farm and (2) the producer, 
although able and willing to pay his pro­
portionate share of the penalty or, in 
accordance with §  728.256 or §  728.257, 
to store or to deliver to the Secretary of 
Agriculture the number of bushels re­
quired to postpone or avoid the payment 
of such proportionate share, is unable 
to arrange with the other wheat pro-
1  Supp. No. 1 appears at 6 F.R. 3465. 
*6 FU. 2701.
ducers on the farm, within thirty calen­
dar days after the threshing of the 1941 
crop of wheat on the farm is completed, 
for the payment of the penalty on the 
entire farm marketing excess or the dis­
position of such farm marketing excess.
Section 728.265 is amended to read as 
follows:
§  728.265 Records to be kept and re­
ports to be made by producers.  Each 
person who in 1941 harvests wheat which 
is subject to the provisions of these regu­
lations shall, in conformity with section 
373 (b) of the Act, keep the records and 
make the reports prescribed by this sec­
tion, which the Secretary of Agriculture 
hereby finds to be necessary to enable 
him to carry out, with respect to wheat, 
the provisions of Title III of the Act and 
of the Resolution. The operator of each 
farm in connection with which a farm 
marketing excess is determined and for 
which a marketing card is not issued un­
der §  728.240 or §  728.271 or §  728.272 
shall file with the treasurer of the county 
committee for the county in which the 
farm is located a report on form Wheat 
519 showing for the farm the follow­
ing information: (a) the total number 
of bushels of wheat produced thereon in 
1941, (b) the name and address of each 
buyer or transferee of any wheat, (c) the 
amount of wheat marketed to him, (d) 
the amount equivalent to the penalty 
which was deducted from the price or 
consideration received for the wheat, (e) 
the amount of unmarketed wheat of the 
1941 crop on hand, and (f ) the acreage of 
wheat. The report in connection with 
any such farm shall be made not later 
than Sixty calendar days next succeeding 
the day on which the threshing of wheat 
produced on the farm is completed, or 
December 31, 1941, whichever is the 
earlier. Upon the, request of the county 
committee, the operator of any other 
farm shall make a similar report within 
15 days after the request therefor is 
made. (Sec. 373 (b),' 52 Stat. 65, 7  
U.S.C. 1373 ( b ) )
Done at Washington, D. C., this 8th day 
of September, 1941. Witness my hand 
and the seal of the Department of Agri­
culture.

general soil-depleting base will be determined as follows:
The county committee, subject to the approval of the State  
committee, will designate the major soil-depleting crop in

designate two alternate major soil-depleting crops from  
among the crops for which the county yield data are avail­

shall remain in force until revoked by the President or by act 
o f Congress.

{"actor_id":"EO:8861","char_end":18582,"char_start":17704,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"on_signing","effective_date":"1941-08-20","effective_wording":[{"char_end":17623,"char_start":16068,"text":"Doc. 41-6242; Filed, August 21, 1941;  \n9:27 a. m.]\nEXECUTIVE ORDER\nS uspending  the  P rovisions  of the  S at­\nurday H alf-H oliday A ct of M arch 3,  \n1931, as to C ertain  E mployees  of the  \nF ederal G overnment  in  the  T erri ­\ntory  of H awaii\nWHEREAS section 5 (a) of the act of  \nJune 28, 1940, 54 Stat. 676, 678, author­\nizes the President “to suspend, in whole  \nor in part, for the War and Navy Depart­\nments and for the Coast Guard and their  \nfield services, during the period of the  \nnational emergency declared by him on  \nSeptember 8, 1939,1  to exist, the provi­\nsions of the act of March 3, 1931 (46  \nStat. 1482; U.S.C. 5, 26 (a)), if in his  \njudgment such course is necessary in the  \ninterest of national defense”, such pro­\nvisions in effect, establishing Saturday  \nhalf-holidays for certain Government  \nemployees; and\nWHEREAS I find it necessary in the  \ninterest of national defense to suspend  \nthe provisions of the said act of March  \n3, 1931, as to certain employees of the  \nGovernment to which section 5 (a) of  \nthe said act of June 28, 1940, is appli­\ncable:\nNOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  \nauthority vested in my by section 5 (a)  \nof the said act of June 28, 1940,1 hereby  \nsuspend for the duration of the national  \nemergency declared by me on September  \n8, 1939, to exist, the provisions of the  \nsaid act of March 3, 1931, as to all civil  \nemployees of the War Department and  \nof the Coast Guard and of their field  \nservices engaged in the performance of  \nlabor or duties in the Territory of  \nHawaii."},{"char_end":35288,"char_start":34417,"text":"Except as the shipment of  \ngrapes may be regulated pursuant to sec­\ntion 951.5, grapes shipped immediately '  \nafter removal from such a warehouse  \nshall meet the grade or size requirements  \nof the applicable regulatioh in effect at  \nthe time such grapes were placed in such  \nwarehouse, and, in the event such grapes  \nwere inspected pursuant to §  951.4 (d)  \nprior to or at the time they were placed  \nin such warehouse, no further inspection  \nunder §  951.4 (d) shall be required: Pro­\nvided, That, unless such grapes meet the  \nrequirements of the regulation applicable  \nto grapes shipped to destinations on the  \ncontinent of North America which is in  \neffect at the time of shipment from such  \nwarehouse, such grapes shall have been  \nin such warehouse for such period of  \ntime as the Industry Committee may pre­\nscribe with the approval of the Secretary."},{"char_end":42032,"char_start":41511,"text":"At the time  \nof making such recommendation, the  \nIndustry Committee shall report to the  \nSecretary (i) the period during which  \nthe proposed regulation is to be effective;  \n(ii) the expected maximum and average  \ndaily shipments of grapes during such  \nperiod; (iii) the total quantity of grapes  \nadvisable to be shipped each day during  \nthe regulation period; and (iv) the infor­\nmation upon which such recommenda­\ntion and reports are based, together with  \nsuch other information as the Secretary  \nmay request."},{"char_end":44216,"char_start":43993,"text":"The provisions of this  \nparagraph shall not be applicable to  \ngrapes which have been shipped in rail­\nroad cars at a time when a regulation  \nperiod established pursuant to paragraph \n(c) of this section is not in effect."},{"char_end":44865,"char_start":44243,"text":"During the  \neffective period of any regulation estab­\nlished pursuant to this section, each  \nhandler shall report promptly, or cause  \nto be reported promptly, to the Industry  \nCommittee any of the following informa­\ntion, requested by it: (1) the quantity of  \ngrapes loaded in railroad cars for ship­\nment to any railroad assembly point; (2)  \nthe date of the bill of lading covering  \neach such carload of grapes; (3) the  \nquantity of grapes loaded in a conveyance \nfor shipment to* assembly points or de­\nlivered to assembly points; and (4) the  \ntime of delivery of each carload of grapes  \nat any assembly point."},{"char_end":53448,"char_start":52377,"text":"In that event, the release of  \nsuch grapes from cold storage for con­\ntinued shipment shall be in the same or­\nder that such grapes were placed, in  \nstorage, and within the limits of the  \nquantity of grapes advisable to be re­\nleased that day, less the quantity eligible \nfor release from assembly points: Pro­\nvided, That any quantity of grapes in  \ncold storage may be substituted, pursu­\nant to the regulations adopted by the  \nIndustry Committee, for the same quan­\ntity of grapes eligible to be released from  \nassembly points, or from cold storage  \npursuant to the.foregoing provisions, ex­\ncept that grapes which have not been  \nin cold storage at least ten (10) days  \nshall not be so released unless such  \ngrapes were delivered to cold storage  \nwhen no limitation period established  \npursuant to (g) (3) or (5) of this sec­\ntion was in effect and such grapes meet  \nthe requirements of the grade and size  \nregulations applicable to grapes shipped  \nto destinations on the continent of North  \nAmerica and in effect at the time such  \ngrapes are released."},{"char_end":55051,"char_start":54441,"text":"(2) At the time of making any such  \nrecommendation, the Industry Com­\nmittee shall determine and report to the  \nSecretary (i) the daily shipments of  \ngrapes to assembly points immediately  \npreceding such recommendation; (ii) the  \ntotal quantity of grapes at assembly  \npoints; (iii) the estimated total quantity  \nof grapes that will be en route to, and at,  \nassembly points on the day the regula­\ntion of loading or packaging is recom­\nmended to be effective; (iv) all other in­\nformation upon which such recommenda­\ntion and report are based; and (v) such  \ninformation as the Secretary may .re­\nquest."},{"char_end":56530,"char_start":55925,"text":"(3) Whenever the Secretary shall  \nfind, from the recommendation, reports,  \nand information submitted by the Indus­\ntry Committee, or from other available  \ninformation, that to limit the loading of  \ngrapes for shipment to assembly points  \nduring a specified period will tend to ef­\nfectuate the declared policy of the act,  \nthe Secretary shall limit the quantity of  \ngrapes to be loaded, during each day of  \na specified period, for shipment to as­\nsembly points: Provided, That no regula­\ntion which limits completely such load­\ning of grapes shall be in effect for a  \nperiod longer than 48 hours."},{"char_end":62742,"char_start":62580,"text":"(1) Whenever a  \nregulation limiting the packaging of  \ngrapes is in effect pursuant to §  951.5(g) \n(5), no handler shall package grapes for  \nshipment by truck."},{"char_end":63501,"char_start":62999,"text":"(2) The Industry Committee shall is­\nsue a permit to any handler which will  \nenable such handler to load and trans­\nport grapes by truck during a regulation  \nperiod limiting the packaging of grapes,  \nestablished pursuant to §  951.5 (g) (5):  \nProvided,  That such handler (i) makes  \nwritten application for such permit; and  \n(ii) submits evidence satisfactory to the  \nIndustry Committee that the grapes to  \nbe shipped had been packaged prior to  \nthe effective time of such regulation pe­\nriod."},{"char_end":64777,"char_start":63632,"text":"(3) In the event the Secretary estab­\nlishes a regulation limiting the loading  \nof grapes pursuant to §  951.5 (g) (3),  \nno handler shall ship grapes by truck,  \nduring any day of such limitation period, \nin excess of the average daily quantity  \nof grapes which such handler shipped by  \ntruck during such period of time during  \nthe then current season as shall be es­\ntablished by the Industry Committee and \napproved by the Secretary; except that  \nany such handler may ship during any  \nday or days during the effective period  \nof the regulation a total of the quantities  \nwhich, pursuant to the foregoing pro­\nvision, he would be permitted to ship  \neach day of such period: Provided, That \na handler who ships by truck, and who  \nhas made no shipments during a particu­\nlar season prior to the effective date of  \na regulation limiting the loading of  \ngrapes, may apply to the said committee  \nfor a certificate (which shall be issued  \nby said committee in accordance with  \nrules adopted by it and approved by the  \nSecretary) which will permit such han­\ndler to ship by truck during the appli­\ncable regulation period an equitable"},{"char_end":66220,"char_start":65599,"text":"In witness whereof, the undersigned,  \nacting under the provisions of Public  \nAct No. 10, 73d Congress, {"actor_id":"EO:8861","char_end":18582,"char_start":17704,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"on_signing","effective_date":"1941-08-20","effective_wording":[{"char_end":17623,"char_start":16068,"text":"Doc. 41-6242; Filed, August 21, 1941;  \n9:27 a. m.]\nEXECUTIVE ORDER\nS uspending  the  P rovisions  of the  S at­\nurday H alf-H oliday A ct of M arch 3,  \n1931, as to C ertain  E mployees  of the  \nF ederal G overnment  in  the  T erri ­\ntory  of H awaii\nWHEREAS section 5 (a) of the act of  \nJune 28, 1940, 54 Stat. 676, 678, author­\nizes the President “to suspend, in whole  \nor in part, for the War and Navy Depart­\nments and for the Coast Guard and their  \nfield services, during the period of the  \nnational emergency declared by him on  \nSeptember 8, 1939,1  to exist, the provi­\nsions of the act of March 3, 1931 (46  \nStat. 1482; U.S.C. 5, 26 (a)), if in his  \njudgment such course is necessary in the  \ninterest of national defense”, such pro­\nvisions in effect, establishing Saturday  \nhalf-holidays for certain Government  \nemployees; and\nWHEREAS I find it necessary in the  \ninterest of national defense to suspend  \nthe provisions of the said act of March  \n3, 1931, as to certain employees of the  \nGovernment to which section 5 (a) of  \nthe said act of June 28, 1940, is appli­\ncable:\nNOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  \nauthority vested in my by section 5 (a)  \nof the said act of June 28, 1940,1 hereby  \nsuspend for the duration of the national  \nemergency declared by me on September  \n8, 1939, to exist, the provisions of the  \nsaid act of March 3, 1931, as to all civil  \nemployees of the War Department and  \nof the Coast Guard and of their field  \nservices engaged in the performance of  \nlabor or duties in the Territory of  \nHawaii."},{"char_end":35288,"char_start":34417,"text":"Except as the shipment of  \ngrapes may be regulated pursuant to sec­\ntion 951.5, grapes shipped immediately '  \nafter removal from such a warehouse  \nshall meet the grade or size requirements  \nof the applicable regulatioh in effect at  \nthe time such grapes were placed in such  \nwarehouse, and, in the event such grapes  \nwere inspected pursuant to §  951.4 (d)  \nprior to or at the time they were placed  \nin such warehouse, no further inspection  \nunder §  951.4 (d) shall be required: Pro­\nvided, That, unless such grapes meet the  \nrequirements of the regulation applicable  \nto grapes shipped to destinations on the  \ncontinent of North America which is in  \neffect at the time of shipment from such  \nwarehouse, such grapes shall have been  \nin such warehouse for such period of  \ntime as the Industry Committee may pre­\nscribe with the approval of the Secretary."},{"char_end":42032,"char_start":41511,"text":"At the time  \nof making such recommendation, the  \nIndustry Committee shall report to the  \nSecretary (i) the period during which  \nthe proposed regulation is to be effective;  \n(ii) the expected maximum and average  \ndaily shipments of grapes during such  \nperiod; (iii) the total quantity of grapes  \nadvisable to be shipped each day during  \nthe regulation period; and (iv) the infor­\nmation upon which such recommenda­\ntion and reports are based, together with  \nsuch other information as the Secretary  \nmay request."},{"char_end":44216,"char_start":43993,"text":"The provisions of this  \nparagraph shall not be applicable to  \ngrapes which have been shipped in rail­\nroad cars at a time when a regulation  \nperiod established pursuant to paragraph \n(c) of this section is not in effect."},{"char_end":44865,"char_start":44243,"text":"During the  \neffective period of any regulation estab­\nlished pursuant to this section, each  \nhandler shall report promptly, or cause  \nto be reported promptly, to the Industry  \nCommittee any of the following informa­\ntion, requested by it: (1) the quantity of  \ngrapes loaded in railroad cars for ship­\nment to any railroad assembly point; (2)  \nthe date of the bill of lading covering  \neach such carload of grapes; (3) the  \nquantity of grapes loaded in a conveyance \nfor shipment to* assembly points or de­\nlivered to assembly points; and (4) the  \ntime of delivery of each carload of grapes  \nat any assembly point."},{"char_end":53448,"char_start":52377,"text":"In that event, the release of  \nsuch grapes from cold storage for con­\ntinued shipment shall be in the same or­\nder that such grapes were placed, in  \nstorage, and within the limits of the  \nquantity of grapes advisable to be re­\nleased that day, less the quantity eligible \nfor release from assembly points: Pro­\nvided, That any quantity of grapes in  \ncold storage may be substituted, pursu­\nant to the regulations adopted by the  \nIndustry Committee, for the same quan­\ntity of grapes eligible to be released from  \nassembly points, or from cold storage  \npursuant to the.foregoing provisions, ex­\ncept that grapes which have not been  \nin cold storage at least ten (10) days  \nshall not be so released unless such  \ngrapes were delivered to cold storage  \nwhen no limitation period established  \npursuant to (g) (3) or (5) of this sec­\ntion was in effect and such grapes meet  \nthe requirements of the grade and size  \nregulations applicable to grapes shipped  \nto destinations on the continent of North  \nAmerica and in effect at the time such  \ngrapes are released."},{"char_end":55051,"char_start":54441,"text":"(2) At the time of making any such  \nrecommendation, the Industry Com­\nmittee shall determine and report to the  \nSecretary (i) the daily shipments of  \ngrapes to assembly points immediately  \npreceding such recommendation; (ii) the  \ntotal quantity of grapes at assembly  \npoints; (iii) the estimated total quantity  \nof grapes that will be en route to, and at,  \nassembly points on the day the regula­\ntion of loading or packaging is recom­\nmended to be effective; (iv) all other in­\nformation upon which such recommenda­\ntion and report are based; and (v) such  \ninformation as the Secretary may .re­\nquest."},{"char_end":56530,"char_start":55925,"text":"(3) Whenever the Secretary shall  \nfind, from the recommendation, reports,  \nand information submitted by the Indus­\ntry Committee, or from other available  \ninformation, that to limit the loading of  \ngrapes for shipment to assembly points  \nduring a specified period will tend to ef­\nfectuate the declared policy of the act,  \nthe Secretary shall limit the quantity of  \ngrapes to be loaded, during each day of  \na specified period, for shipment to as­\nsembly points: Provided, That no regula­\ntion which limits completely such load­\ning of grapes shall be in effect for a  \nperiod longer than 48 hours."},{"char_end":62742,"char_start":62580,"text":"(1) Whenever a  \nregulation limiting the packaging of  \ngrapes is in effect pursuant to §  951.5(g) \n(5), no handler shall package grapes for  \nshipment by truck."},{"char_end":63501,"char_start":62999,"text":"(2) The Industry Committee shall is­\nsue a permit to any handler which will  \nenable such handler to load and trans­\nport grapes by truck during a regulation  \nperiod limiting the packaging of grapes,  \nestablished pursuant to §  951.5 (g) (5):  \nProvided,  That such handler (i) makes  \nwritten application for such permit; and  \n(ii) submits evidence satisfactory to the  \nIndustry Committee that the grapes to  \nbe shipped had been packaged prior to  \nthe effective time of such regulation pe­\nriod."},{"char_end":64777,"char_start":63632,"text":"(3) In the event the Secretary estab­\nlishes a regulation limiting the loading  \nof grapes pursuant to §  951.5 (g) (3),  \nno handler shall ship grapes by truck,  \nduring any day of such limitation period, \nin excess of the average daily quantity  \nof grapes which such handler shipped by  \ntruck during such period of time during  \nthe then current season as shall be es­\ntablished by the Industry Committee and \napproved by the Secretary; except that  \nany such handler may ship during any  \nday or days during the effective period  \nof the regulation a total of the quantities  \nwhich, pursuant to the foregoing pro­\nvision, he would be permitted to ship  \neach day of such period: Provided, That \na handler who ships by truck, and who  \nhas made no shipments during a particu­\nlar season prior to the effective date of  \na regulation limiting the loading of  \ngrapes, may apply to the said committee  \nfor a certificate (which shall be issued  \nby said committee in accordance with  \nrules adopted by it and approved by the  \nSecretary) which will permit such han­\ndler to ship by truck during the appli­\ncable regulation period an equitable"},{"char_end":66220,"char_start":65599,"text":"In witness whereof, the undersigned,  \nacting under the provisions of Public  \nAct No. 10, 73d Congress, as amended  \nand as reenacted and amended by the  \nAgricultural Marketing Agreement Act  \nof 1937, as amended, for the purposes  \nand within the limitations therein con­\ntained and not otherwise, does hereby  \nexecute and issue in duplicate this order  \nunder his hand and the official seal of  \nthe Department of Agriculture, in the  \ncity of Washington, District of Columbia,  \non this 20th day of August 1941, and de­\nclares this order to be effective on and  \nafter 12:01 a. m., p. s. t., August 24, 1941.\n[seal!"},{"char_end":91616,"char_start":91181,"text":"Order 3651, is Nationality Act of 1940  \nsee 8 CFR, part 112."},{"char_end":109550,"char_start":108123,"text":"Doc. 41-6254; Filed, August 21, 1941;  \n9:57 a. m.J\nTITLE 30— MINERAL RESOURCES\nCHAPTER m —BITUMINOUS COAL \nDIVISION \n[Docket No. A-595]\nP art 324—M inim u m P rice S chedule , \nD istrict  N o. 4\nORDER OF THE DIRECTOR GRANTING PERMA­\nNENT RELIEF IN  PART IN  THE MATTER OF \nTHE PETITION OF WUKELIC COAL COMPANY, \nTERAMANA BROTHERS COAL COMPANY, AND \nCARMAN COAL COMPANY FOR SPECIAL RE­\nLIEF UNDER THE PROVISIONS OF PRICE IN ­\nSTRUCTION NO. 9 OF SUPPLEMENT NO. 1 \nTO PRICE SCHEDULE NO. 1 FOR DISTRICT \nNO. 4\nAn original petition, pursuant to sec­\ntion 4 II (d) and Price Instruction No. 9  \nof the Schedule of Effective Minimum  \nPrices for District No. 4 For All Ship­\nments Except Truck, as amended, which  \nprovides that in proper cases permission  \nmay be granted to code members to add  \nless than the actual cost of transportation  \nto the minimum f. o. b. mine price, hav­\ning been duly filed with the Bituminous  \nCoal Division on January 15, 1941, by the  \nWukelic Coal Company,  Teramana  \nBrothers Coal Company, and Carman  \nCoal Company, code members in District  \nNo. 4, requesting permission to absorb  \nall costs of haulage on mine run coal in  \nexcess of 150 from petitioners’  mines to  \nthe plant of the Kaul Clay Company in  \nToronto, Ohio; and\n1  For regulations with respect to admission  \nof holder of certificate of identity issued  \nunder section 503 of the Nationality Act of  \n1940 see 8 CFB, part 112."},{"char_end":111094,"char_start":109794,"text":"C., at which all inter­\nested parties were afforded an opportu­\nnity to be present, adduce evidence,  \ncross-examine witnesses and otherwise  \nbe heard; and\nTemporary relief having been granted  \nafter an informal conference, pending  \nfinal disposition of the original petition  \nby Order of the Directer dated February  \n18, 1941 ;*  and\nThe preparation and filing of a report  \nby the Examiner having been waived and  \nthe matter submitted to the Director;  \nand\nThe Director having made Findings  \nof Fact1  and Conclusions of Law and  \nrendered an Opinion in this matter  \nwhich are filed herewith;\nNow, therefore, it is ordered,  That  \n§  324.21 (Price instructions and excep­\ntions)  in the Schedule of Effective Mini­\nmum Prices for District No. 4 For Truck  \nShipments only should be amended by  \nthe addition of the following exception  \nto Price Instruction 6 thereof:\nException:  Where coals from the - **ACT:EO:4430>EO:8861@afb4f50b4e620f48**; S410058358479d6a926a77a3e; {"actor_id":"EO:8861","char_end":18582,"char_start":17704,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"on_signing","effective_date":"1941-08-20","effective_wording":[{"char_end":17623,"char_start":16068,"text":"Doc. 41-6242; Filed, August 21, 1941;  \n9:27 a. m.]\nEXECUTIVE ORDER\nS uspending  the  P rovisions  of the  S at­\nurday H alf-H oliday A ct of M arch 3,  \n1931, as to C ertain  E mployees  of the  \nF ederal G overnment  in  the  T erri ­\ntory  of H awaii\nWHEREAS section 5 (a) of the act of  \nJune 28, 1940, 54 Stat. 676, 678, author­\nizes the President “to suspend, in whole  \nor in part, for the War and Navy Depart­\nments and for the Coast Guard and their  \nfield services, during the period of the  \nnational emergency declared by him on  \nSeptember 8, 1939,1  to exist, the provi­\nsions of the act of March 3, 1931 (46  \nStat. 1482; U.S.C. 5, 26 (a)), if in his  \njudgment such course is necessary in the  \ninterest of national defense”, such pro­\nvisions in effect, establishing Saturday  \nhalf-holidays for certain Government  \nemployees; and\nWHEREAS I find it necessary in the  \ninterest of national defense to suspend  \nthe provisions of the said act of March  \n3, 1931, as to certain employees of the  \nGovernment to which section 5 (a) of  \nthe said act of June 28, 1940, is appli­\ncable:\nNOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  \nauthority vested in my by section 5 (a)  \nof the said act of June 28, 1940,1 hereby  \nsuspend for the duration of the national  \nemergency declared by me on September  \n8, 1939, to exist, the provisions of the  \nsaid act of March 3, 1931, as to all civil  \nemployees of the War Department and  \nof the Coast Guard and of their field  \nservices engaged in the performance of  \nlabor or duties in the Territory of  \nHawaii."},{"char_end":35288,"char_start":34417,"text":"Except as the shipment of  \ngrapes may be regulated pursuant to sec­\ntion 951.5, grapes shipped immediately '  \nafter removal from such a warehouse  \nshall meet the grade or size requirements  \nof the applicable regulatioh in effect at  \nthe time such grapes were placed in such  \nwarehouse, and, in the event such grapes  \nwere inspected pursuant to §  951.4 (d)  \nprior to or at the time they were placed  \nin such warehouse, no further inspection  \nunder §  951.4 (d) shall be required: Pro­\nvided, That, unless such grapes meet the  \nrequirements of the regulation applicable  \nto grapes shipped to destinations on the  \ncontinent of North America which is in  \neffect at the time of shipment from such  \nwarehouse, such grapes shall have been  \nin such warehouse for such period of  \ntime as the Industry Committee may pre­\nscribe with the approval of the Secretary."},{"char_end":42032,"char_start":41511,"text":"At the time  \nof making such recommendation, the  \nIndustry Committee shall report to the  \nSecretary (i) the period during which  \nthe proposed regulation is to be effective;  \n(ii) the expected maximum and average  \ndaily shipments of grapes during such  \nperiod; (iii) the total quantity of grapes  \nadvisable to be shipped each day during  \nthe regulation period; and (iv) the infor­\nmation upon which such recommenda­\ntion and reports are based, together with  \nsuch other information as the Secretary  \nmay request."},{"char_end":44216,"char_start":43993,"text":"The provisions of this  \nparagraph shall not be applicable to  \ngrapes which have been shipped in rail­\nroad cars at a time when a regulation  \nperiod established pursuant to paragraph \n(c) of this section is not in effect."},{"char_end":44865,"char_start":44243,"text":"During the  \neffective period of any regulation estab­\nlished pursuant to this section, each  \nhandler shall report promptly, or cause  \nto be reported promptly, to the Industry  \nCommittee any of the following informa­\ntion, requested by it: (1) the quantity of  \ngrapes loaded in railroad cars for ship­\nment to any railroad assembly point; (2)  \nthe date of the bill of lading covering  \neach such carload of grapes; (3) the  \nquantity of grapes loaded in a conveyance \nfor shipment to* assembly points or de­\nlivered to assembly points; and (4) the  \ntime of delivery of each carload of grapes  \nat any assembly point."},{"char_end":53448,"char_start":52377,"text":"In that event, the release of  \nsuch grapes from cold storage for con­\ntinued shipment shall be in the same or­\nder that such grapes were placed, in  \nstorage, and within the limits of the  \nquantity of grapes advisable to be re­\nleased that day, less the quantity eligible \nfor release from assembly points: Pro­\nvided, That any quantity of grapes in  \ncold storage may be substituted, pursu­\nant to the regulations adopted by the  \nIndustry Committee, for the same quan­\ntity of grapes eligible to be released from  \nassembly points, or from cold storage  \npursuant to the.foregoing provisions, ex­\ncept that grapes which have not been  \nin cold storage at least ten (10) days  \nshall not be so released unless such  \ngrapes were delivered to cold storage  \nwhen no limitation period established  \npursuant to (g) (3) or (5) of this sec­\ntion was in effect and such grapes meet  \nthe requirements of the grade and size  \nregulations applicable to grapes shipped  \nto destinations on the continent of North  \nAmerica and in effect at the time such  \ngrapes are released."},{"char_end":55051,"char_start":54441,"text":"(2) At the time of making any such  \nrecommendation, the Industry Com­\nmittee shall determine and report to the  \nSecretary (i) the daily shipments of  \ngrapes to assembly points immediately  \npreceding such recommendation; (ii) the  \ntotal quantity of grapes at assembly  \npoints; (iii) the estimated total quantity  \nof grapes that will be en route to, and at,  \nassembly points on the day the regula­\ntion of loading or packaging is recom­\nmended to be effective; (iv) all other in­\nformation upon which such recommenda­\ntion and report are based; and (v) such  \ninformation as the Secretary may .re­\nquest."},{"char_end":56530,"char_start":55925,"text":"(3) Whenever the Secretary shall  \nfind, from the recommendation, reports,  \nand information submitted by the Indus­\ntry Committee, or from other available  \ninformation, that to limit the loading of  \ngrapes for shipment to assembly points  \nduring a specified period will tend to ef­\nfectuate the declared policy of the act,  \nthe Secretary shall limit the quantity of  \ngrapes to be loaded, during each day of  \na specified period, for shipment to as­\nsembly points: Provided, That no regula­\ntion which limits completely such load­\ning of grapes shall be in effect for a  \nperiod longer than 48 hours."},{"char_end":62742,"char_start":62580,"text":"(1) Whenever a  \nregulation limiting the packaging of  \ngrapes is in effect pursuant to §  951.5(g) \n(5), no handler shall package grapes for  \nshipment by truck."},{"char_end":63501,"char_start":62999,"text":"(2) The Industry Committee shall is­\nsue a permit to any handler which will  \nenable such handler to load and trans­\nport grapes by truck during a regulation  \nperiod limiting the packaging of grapes,  \nestablished pursuant to §  951.5 (g) (5):  \nProvided,  That such handler (i) makes  \nwritten application for such permit; and  \n(ii) submits evidence satisfactory to the  \nIndustry Committee that the grapes to  \nbe shipped had been packaged prior to  \nthe effective time of such regulation pe­\nriod."},{"char_end":64777,"char_start":63632,"text":"(3) In the event the Secretary estab­\nlishes a regulation limiting the loading  \nof grapes pursuant to §  951.5 (g) (3),  \nno handler shall ship grapes by truck,  \nduring any day of such limitation period, \nin excess of the average daily quantity  \nof grapes which such handler shipped by  \ntruck during such period of time during  \nthe then current season as shall be es­\ntablished by the Industry Committee and \napproved by the Secretary; except that  \nany such handler may ship during any  \nday or days during the effective - **ACT:EO:6910>EO:7373@0f7b26ff90712ccf**; S1ee3f8cf6cae97f9736900ee; {"actor_id":"EO:7373","char_end":2762,"char_start":2549,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"agency_variable","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":3336,"char_start":3116,"text":"EFFECTIVE DATE AND GEOGRAPHICAL SCOPE\nArticle\nEffective date of the tax --------------------------------------------------------- 1\nGeographical scope of applicability o f tax ---------------------------- 2\nC H APTER II."},{"char_end":13576,"char_start":13318,"text":"E f fec tive D ate  of  t h e T a x.— The capital stock \ntax imposed by section 105 of the Revenue Act of 1935 ap­\nplies with respect to each year ending June 30, beginning  \nwith the year ending June 30, 1936, and is in effect from and  \nafter July 1, 1935."},{"char_end":93049,"char_start":92663,"text":"(For discussion of incomplete returns, see articles  \n31 and 37; for discussion of penalties and interest, see  \narticles 81 and 82.)\nIf the claim for exemption relates to a return upon which  \nthe corporation made an original declaration of value for  \nits capital stock and the claim is allowed, such declaration  \ndoes not become effective as the statutory original declared  \nvalue."},{"char_end":178356,"char_start":177988,"text":"S ervice  and  R eg u lat o r y A n n o u n c e m e n t s\nFOOD AND DRUG NO. 4, THIRD REVISION, SUPPLEMENT NO. 2\nUnder the authority conferred by the amendment of July 8,  \n1930, to the Federal Food and Drugs Act (sec. 8, par. 5, in  \nthe case of food), there is hereby promulgated, to become  \neffective 90 days from date, a revision of the standard for  \ncanned peas."},{"char_end":197843,"char_start":196934,"text":"Temporary exemption from Sections 12  (a ) \nand 7 (c) (2) of certain evidences of indebtedness of certain  \nforeign states; prohibition of use of manipulative or deceptive  \ndevices or contrivances with respect thereto . — (a) Evidences \nof indebtedness (i) which have been issued by any foreign  \nstate that is presently governed by an interim government  \nwhich is holding office temporarily and which is to continue  \nto hold such office only until the assumption thereof by a  \nregular government which has been elected and (ii) as to  \nwhich temporary exemption from the operation of Section  \n12 (a) shall expire pursuant to the terms of Rule AN7 on  \nMay 15, 1936, and as to which registration shall not be  \neffective on that date, shall be exempt from the operation  \nof said Section 12 (a) to and including the thirtieth day  \nfollowing the assumption of office by such elected regular  \ngovernment."},{"char_end":199360,"char_start":199278,"text":"This Rule shall be effective immediately upon publication.  \n[ se al] F r ancis P."},{"char_end":200731,"char_start":200640,"text":"The foregoing rule shall be effective immediately upon  \npublication.\n[ se al] F r ancis P."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:6910>EO:7373@0f7b26ff90712ccf","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending asserted. Effective date depends on agency, publication or an unstated event.","provision_label":"","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":["(2) Mutual savings banks not having a capital stock  \nrepresented by shares;\n(3) Fraternal beneficiary societies, orders, or associations,  \n(A ) operating under the lodge system or for the exclusive  \nbenefit of the members of a fraternity itself operating  \nunder the lodge system; and (B ) providing for the pay­\nment of life, sick, accident, or other benefits to the mem­\nbers of such society, order, or association or their  \ndependents;\n(4) Domestic building and loan associations substantially  \nall the business of which is confined to making loans to  \nmembers; and cooperative banks without capital stock  \norganized and operated for mutual purposes and <  without  \nprofit;\n(5) Cemetery companies owned and operated exclusively  \nfor the benefit of their members or which are not operated  \nfor profit; and any corporation chartered solely for burial  \npurposes as a cemetery corporation and not permitted by  \nits charter to engage in any business not necessarily inci­\ndent to that purpose, no part of the net earnings of  \nwhich inures to the benefit of any private shareholder or  \nindividual;\n(6) Corporations, and any community chest, fund, or  \nfoundation, organized and operated exclusively for religious,  \ncharitable, scientific, literary, or educational purposes, or  \nfor the prevention of cruelty to children or animals, no  \npart of the net earnings of which inures to the benefit of any  \nprivate shareholder or individual, and no substantial part  \nof the activities of which 4s carrying on propaganda, or  \notherwise attempting, to influence legislation;\n(7) Business leagues, chambers of commerce, real-estate  \nboards, or boards of trade, not organized for profit and no  \npart of the net earnings of which inures to the benefit of  \nany private shareholder or individual;\n(8) Civic leagues or organizations not organized for profit  \nbut operated exclusively for the promotion of social welfare,  \nor local associations of employees, the membership of which  \nis limited to the employees of a designated person or per­\nsons in a particular municipality, and the net earnings of  \nwhich are devoted exclusively to charitable, educational,  \nor recreational purposes;\n(9) Clubs organized and operated exclusively for pleasure,  \nrecreation, and other nonprofitable purposes, no part of the  \nnet earnings of . ,  which inures to the benefit of any private  \nshareholder;\n(10) Benevolent life insurance associations of a purely  \nlocal character, mutual ditch or irrigation companies, mu­\ntual or cooperative telephone companies, or like organiza­\ntions; but only if 85 per centum or more of the income  \nconsists of amounts collected from members for the sole  \npurpose of meeting losses and expenses;\n(11) Farmers’ or other mutual hail, cyclone, casualty, or  \nfire insurance companies or associations (including inter-  \ninsurers and reciprocal underwriters) the income of which  \nis used or held for the purpose Of paying losses or expenses;\n(12) Farmers’, fruit growers’, or like associations organized  \nand operated on a cooperative basis (a) for the purpose of  \nmarketing the products of members or other producers, and  \nturning back to them the proceeds of sales, less the necessary  \nmarketing expenses, on the basis of either the quantity or  \nthe value of the products furnished by them, or (b ) for the  \npurpose of purchasing supplies and equipment for the use  \nof members or other persons, and turning over such supplies  \nand equipment to them at actual cost, plus necessary ex­\npenses."],"scope":"whole","signing_date":null,"target_id":"EO:6910","verb":"supersede"}

otherwise is made \nsubject to competitive examination shall, j \nupon recommendation to the Commis­\nsion by the head of the department or \nagency in which he is employed have all \nthe rights which he would have acquired \nif appointed thereto by competitive ex­\namination: Provided:  (a) That he has \nrendered six months of satisfactory ac­\ntive service in the civilian executive \nbranch of the Federal Government im­\nmediately prior to the effective date of \nthe change in status of the position, and \ncontinues to serve in such position for 60 \ndays thereafter; (b) that he shall pass \nsuch appropriate noncompetitive tests of \nfitness as the Commission may prescribe; \nand (c) that he is not disqualified by any \nprovision of section 3 of Civil Service \nRule V or of any other civil service rule \nor by any provision of the Civil Service \nAct or any other statute or executive \norder: Provided further,  that in con­\nferring a classified competitive status \nupon any employee under this or any \nother rule or any statute or executive \norder, the Commission (a) may, in its \ndiscretion, exempt from the physical re­\nquirements established for any position \nany employee who has rendered long and \nfaithful service in a civil capacity for \nthe Government, and (b) may consider a \nperson whose name is carried on the \ncompensation rolls of the Employees’ \nCompensation Commission as having \nrendered satisfactory active service in \nthe position in which he last served for\nthe period which his name is carried on \nsuch rolls."},{"char_end":35568,"char_start":35193,"text":"On the effective date \nof any such order, section 6 of this rule \nshall apply to the positions, officers, and \nemployees of the offices they apply to those in offices \nnow classified."},{"char_end":65237,"char_start":64857,"text":"All shipments \nallowable under these regulations shall \nbegin within six months of the effective egister."},{"char_end":73856,"char_start":73398,"text":"(a) Whenever the Secretary [of \nAgriculture] finds that the total supply of \ntobacco as of the beginning of the marketing \nyear then current exceeds the reserve supply \nlevel therefor, the Secretary shall proclaim \nthe amount of such total supply, and, begin­\nning on the first day of the marketing year \nnext following and continuing throughout \nsuch year, a national marketing quota shall \nbe in effect for the tobacco marketed during \nsuch marketing year."},{"char_end":121818,"char_start":119225,"text":"It appearing,  That by order entered \nJuly 30, 1936, as amended by order en­\ntered October 31, 1938, the Commission \nentered into an investigation in and con­\ncerning the matter of establishing for \nprivate carriers of property engaged in \ninterstate or foreign commerce, if need \ntherefor is found, reasonable require­\nments to promote safety of operation \nand to that end prescribe qualifications \nand maximum hours of service of em­\nployees and standards of equipment;\nIt further appearing,  That a full in­\nvestigation of the matters and things \ninvolved was had and that the Commis­\nsion, Division 5, on May 1, 1940, made \nand filed a report containing its findings \nof fact and conclusions thereon and on \nthe same date entered an order pre­\nscribing regulations to promote the \nsafety of operation by private carriers of \nproperty engaged in interstate or foreign \ncommerce effective August 1, 1940;\nIt further appearing,  That the Com­\nmission, Division 5, by order of July 19, \n1940, postponed the effective date of said \nregulations to October 1, 1940, and by \norder of September 21, 1940, further \npostponed the effective date to October \n15, 1940;\nIt further appearing,  That the Com­\nmission, Division 5, by order entered \nSeptember 30, 1940,1  vacated and set \naside its order of May 1, 1940, and pre­\nscribed regulations to promote safety of \noperation by private carriers engaged in \ninterstate and foreign commerce which \ndiffered in some respects from the regu­\nlations prescribed by the said order of \nMay 1, 1940;\nIt further appearing,  That the Na­\ntional Retail Dry Goods Association filed \na petition requesting modification of cer­\ntain of the rules so prescribed, and that \non the date hereof the Commission, Di­\nvision 5, has made and filed a report \ngranting said petition in part, which re­\nport and said report of May 1, 1940, \ncontaining its findings of fact and con­\nclusions thereon, are hereby referred to \nand made a part hereof ;\nAnd it further appearing,  That said \npetition having been fully considered by \nthe Commission, and good cause there­\nfor appearing;\nIt is ordered, That effective December \n10,1940, said order of September 30,1940, \nbe, and it is hereby, amended so as to \nadd at the end of Rule 3 (a) of the hours \nof service regulations as it applies to \nprivate carriers of property the fol­\nlowing:\nProvided further, however,  That this \nrule shall not apply with respect to driv­\ners of motor vehicles engaged solely in \nmaking deliveries for retail stores during \nthe period from December 10 to Decem­\nber 25, both inclusive, of each year."},{"char_end":139161,"char_start":138762,"text":"If, during the continuance of the lease­\nhold term herein ## Valla review leads and component attestations

Review lead only. Every case needs separate applicability, earlier-ending, scope, independent-command, savings and independent whole-case review.
Preparation attestations never approve legal conclusions or replace whole-case review.
